name: agent-monitor
description: Classifies every terminal window running an AI coding agent as working/waiting/done/idle and marks that window's own PROJECTS-pane row the way Orca does: a spinner, an amber ?, an emerald dot, a red dot for an interrupted turn, a gray dot for idle. Reads the app's own agent list from Settings → AI Providers, with zero-config detection from pane titles and Claude Code transcripts; installing the app's agent hooks there upgrades permission-prompt and done detection to the agent's own events, for every agent in that list rather than Claude Code alone.

agentMonitor.waitingThresholdSeconds.description: How long an agent's transcript can go unwritten before it's shown as done rather than working. Only used when no hook event is fresher (see the extension's README): a single tool call routinely runs longer than a few seconds without writing anything, so a short threshold reports a busy agent as waiting. Install the agent hooks from Settings → AI Providers for the exact answer instead of a timeout.

enumDescriptions: Only agents in the project of the tab you opened the board from.
Only agents in the projects you tick in the board's Selected list.
agentMonitor.board.defaultScope.description: Which agents the AGENTS board shows the first time it opens in a browser. After that the board remembers the scope you last picked in its toolbar, per browser.

agentMonitor.board.pollInterval.description: How often (ms) the AGENTS board refreshes. It refreshes only while its tab is the one on screen: in the background it makes no requests.
